criterion: The public routes sit on a near-white warm neutral ground closer to paper than to white, and the text on them is a deep warm neutral rather than true black.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the home, services and article routes share an off-white warm ground designed as one light mode, and their body text reads as a very dark warm grey. Answer no when the ground is pure white or a cool grey, when body text is pure black, or when the routes are designed dark.

criterion: The hero on the home route is grounded in a light, soft green running edge to edge, and each of the other four accents appears on one thing alone.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the home hero is a full-bleed soft green and the cyan, amber, coral and violet accents each appear on a single element such as one promise tile or the quote action. Answer no when the hero is another colour, or when one surface wears two accents at once.

criterion: An article opened from the article index holds its body to a narrow reading measure of about forty-eight rem rather than running the full width of the grid.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the article body column stays around forty-eight rem wide on a wide screen while the page furniture around it spans further. Answer no when the body text runs the full width of the layout.

criterion: The related-reading block on a method route appears where a published article shares that method's tag, and the following section sits in its place where nothing matches.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a method route with a matching article shows a related article card and a method route with nothing matching moves straight to the next section. Answer no when an empty related-reading heading stands over an empty area.

criterion: The home route and the methodology routes give their subject the room to be seen first, with one dominant thing in view before any surrounding furniture.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the first screen of the home, methodology and article routes leads with one subject given generous space. Answer no when the first screen is a dense arrangement of equal-weight blocks with nothing leading.

criterion: Content loading in place on the article index settles as a card-shaped skeleton at the destination shape.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when results loading into the article grid show card-shaped placeholders of the destination shape. Answer no when a spinner sits in the middle of a collapsed grid.

criterion: Every character on the public site is set in the grotesque Space Grotesk, with body copy at one rem on a handset and one and one sixteenth rem on a wide screen.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when headings and body across the home, methodology and article routes are one grotesque family named Space Grotesk and body copy grows a little between a handset and a wide screen. Answer no when a second family appears outside that stack or when body copy holds one fixed size at every width.

criterion: The hero display on the home route reaches about ten and seven eighths rem on a wide screen, and figures line up on tabular numerals wherever counts stack.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the home hero words fill most of the screen width at that size and the three published figures align digit under digit. Answer no when the hero display stays near body scale or the figures sit on proportional numerals that wander.

criterion: The three published figures on the home route arrive one after another a beat apart, and every entrance resolves at once to its end state for a visitor who asks for reduced motion.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the three figures stagger in on a first read and every element is at its resting position immediately under a reduced-motion preference. Answer no when the figures arrive together, or when content stays hidden under reduced motion because its entrance never runs.

criterion: Looping movement on the home route and the network route holds its first frame for a visitor who asks for reduced motion.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the client mark wall and the country rail stand still under a reduced-motion preference. Answer no when either keeps sliding.

criterion: Body text on the public routes reaches a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1 against its ground, and interface components reach at least 3 to 1.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when body copy on the warm ground and on the green hero, and the borders of form controls on the contact stages, meet those two ratios. Answer no when any of them falls below.

criterion: A heading on the home route or the network route that is split into separate words for its entrance also exists once as a single readable string for assistive technology.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the animated headings on the home and network routes carry a hidden copy reading as one sentence. Answer no when the only copy of such a heading is the per-word one.

criterion: The article index arranges its cards three across on a wide screen.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a wide window shows three article cards to a row. Answer no when the wide window shows one, two or four to a row.

criterion: Layout across the public routes resolves on a sixteen-column grid whose gaps are multiples of one base unit.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the asymmetric splits on the promise tiles and the regional bands line up on a sixteen-column rhythm and the gaps between elements are consistent multiples of one unit. Answer no when the layout resolves on twelve columns or the gaps vary at random.

criterion: The console board opens with a large decorative hero above the opportunity cards.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the console board carries an oversized image or editorial composition above the card grid. Answer no when the board opens straight onto the cards beneath the sidebar.

criterion: The confirmation after a submitted brief promises that a message has been sent by email.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the confirmation page says an email has been sent or is on its way. Answer no when the confirmation names the reference and what happens next on screen alone.

criterion: The footer beneath the articles index offers a control that switches the site into a second language.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a language switcher appears in the chrome of any public route. Answer no when every route reads in one language throughout.
